teaser.text: Weichai Power is an industrial group that sells the machinery behind transport, farming, warehouses and backup power. Its dollar comes in when customers buy equipment, projects, parts and service, and goes out first to build and support those products before the remainder becomes profit.

blocks.heading: Where could Weichai Power's shares go?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast reaches HK$24.19 in October 2027, implying a 0% return including dividends, and HK$29.00 in October 2029, implying a 28% return; the outcome hinges on durable growth, cash conversion, and a mid-cycle valuation.

The valuation is 14.5x trailing P/E and 12.7x forward P/E, with a real free-cash-flow yield of 9.7%. The forecast assigns 25% probability to the bear case, 55% to base, and 20% to bull, producing a final share-price range of HK$13.47 to HK$47.92.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Weichai Power?

paragraphs.text: The first test is whether large-engine and data-centre power orders repeat profitably in 2026, including about 4,000 data-centre backup-engine deliveries. The large-engine project targets readiness in December 2027; orders, utilization, and margins then decide whether capacity earns its projected return. In 2027–29, repeat battery orders and on-time KION backlog delivery support the bull case, while overruns, delayed collections, or weak truck demand push toward bear.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Weichai Power really make?

paragraphs.text: The 2025 picture was much healthier. Operating cash flow reached RMB28,681.5 million, and free cash flow after capital spending, leases and interest was RMB18,907.1 million. Deducting stock compensation produces “real free cash flow” of RMB18,098.2 million, because shares paid to employees still dilute shareholders even without an immediate cash payment.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Weichai Power?

paragraphs.text: At HK$25.42, the trailing P/E is 14.5x. P/E means the share price divided by earnings per share: it tells us how much investors pay for each unit of current profit. But engine earnings move with factory utilisation. Buildings, machinery and staff cost money even when fewer trucks are sold, so profit can rise quickly in a strong market and fall faster than sales in a weak one. A low P/E near the top of that cycle may therefore be less attractive than a higher P/E near the bottom.

blocks.heading: How much does Weichai Power pay per share over time?

paragraphs.text: Weichai then made shareholder returns more explicit. It cancelled 50,252,475 repurchased shares in May 2026. In August, it declared an interim dividend of RMB0.517 per share, while management said the interim payout ratio had risen from 55% to 58%. The conclusion is measurable: Weichai can return cash, but its capital-allocation record will depend on whether delayed projects turn retained and raised money into durable returns.

blocks.heading: Is Weichai Power's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Cash generation recovered in 2023–25. In 2025, free cash flow reached RMB18,907.11306467 million, while shareholder payments were RMB6,878.4802883 million, or 36.4% of free cash flow. Acquisitions required RMB513.71498698 million. Debt repayments exceeded new borrowing, but cash still fell and year-end net cash was RMB22,467.91323486 million, below its 2021 level.

blocks.heading: What could change Weichai Power's dividend?

paragraphs.text: Dividends start at CNY0.99 in the base case, then reach CNY1.08 and CNY1.17. The analyst’s NTM EPS estimate is CNY1.70763, while management said the interim payout ratio rose to 58%. The forecast therefore assumes 9% annual EPS growth, with margins below stronger 2024 levels.

The bear case gives CNY0.75 initially, then CNY0.68 and CNY0.68 as earnings and payout capacity weaken. The bull case gives CNY1.10, CNY1.30 and CNY1.50 as mix and margins improve. The five-year record, including the 2022 cut and later recovery, supports a dividend that is growing but cyclical.
